items.q: Why does the pressure of a gas rise when it is heated at constant volume?
items.correct: Its particles move faster, hitting the walls harder and more often.
items.misconception: The particles themselves expand and take up more room.
items.random_wrong: New gas particles are created by the heat.
items.why: Particles don't expand or multiply. Heating raises their kinetic energy, so wall collisions are harder and more frequent — raising pressure.

items.q: What happens to the temperature while a pure solid is melting?
items.correct: It stays constant — the energy breaks bonds rather than raising temperature.
items.misconception: It keeps rising steadily as you heat it.
items.random_wrong: It drops while the solid melts.
items.why: During a change of state, energy (latent heat) overcomes forces between particles instead of increasing their kinetic energy, so temperature holds steady.

items.q: How are particles arranged in a gas?
items.correct: Far apart, moving quickly in random directions, with negligible forces between them.
items.misconception: Closely packed in a regular pattern, like a solid.
items.random_wrong: In fixed rows that can only vibrate.
items.why: Widely-spaced, randomly-moving particles are why gases fill their container and are easily compressed.
